quote: Good systems don't happen by accident. They are designed, tested and earned.
aboutBody: I didn't start in software. I studied petrochemical technology at Anna University — and somewhere along the way realised the part of every project I actually loved was the code. So I taught myself to build, earned an IBM full-stack certification in Chennai, and never looked back.

Three years later, I've shipped live platforms for a UK fragrance brand, a Doha stationery store, a security firm and a construction company — most of them as the only engineer on the project, from the first database schema to the Nginx config on the server.

The projects I build for myself are the ones that keep me up at night: a DNS shield that protects a whole phone without root, an ERP that keeps working when the internet doesn't, meeting AI that runs entirely on my own hardware. If a system depends on someone else's cloud, my first question is always — does it have to?
Today I lead backend engineering at Holora Performance in Doha. The rule hasn't changed since my first commit: understand the constraint first, and the architecture follows.
